statement: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, then folded in half again, and then folded in half a third time. One hole is punched through all the layers, away from every fold and edge. How many holes are there when the sheet is unfolded?

choices.misconception: I counted one hole for each fold.
I added two holes for each of the three folds.
I counted every hole twice, once on each side of the paper.
I multiplied the 8 layers by the 3 folds.

hints: How many layers does the hole go through?
Each fold in half doubles the number of layers. A single punch makes one hole in every layer, and each layer becomes a separate part of the unfolded sheet.
The layers go 1, then 2, then 4, then 8, so the punch goes through 8 layers.

solutions.reliable: Each fold in half doubles the number of layers: 1 becomes 2, then 4, then 8. A punch away from every fold and edge makes one hole in each layer, and unfolding spreads those layers back across the sheet, so there are 8 separate holes. The transferable idea: folding doubles the layers each time, so after n folds one punch makes n twos multiplied together, which is 8 holes for three folds.

whyOnTest: Folding and punching problems test whether you track layers doubling rather than adding a fixed amount per fold.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
